pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as 3-4 kettlebell sessions a week of 30-40 minutes plus 5-15 minutes of daily mobility targeted at glutes, hips, knees and shoulder, with form checked by video. Prospect took notes and agreed without pushback: 'No, that's pretty good. Yeah. 30 to 43 times a week, which is the kettlebell program. then, yeah, 5-15 minutes. It's daily for mobility and stretching, yeah, absolute must.' He had already pre-sold himself on the modality earlier — 'what I'm attracted to with the program is the natural range of movement'.

Asked how the pillar mechanically works before reacting — 'within your program, do you, like, put dietary suggestions out there where it's like, oh, hey, look, this breakfast, lunch, and dinner sort of thing' — then probed fit with his own practice twice more: 'I always was concerned with wanting to do fasts and being able to integrate that within the system' and 'if you've got a suggestion to have some kind of electrolyte program within that'. Also surfaced a constraint the rep parked rather than solved: 'I don't like veggies, but I'll drink them.'

He had named accountability as the thing he most wanted ('I really like the accountability to answer your question'), but pushed back on the substance of how it is delivered when the community element was presented: 'I'm not so super jazzed with the whole sort of, yeah, I'll be part of the community, you know... See, if I outsource my accountability, I've already lost. I have to, I have to be the one.' He redefined what he would accept — peer-to-peer energy rather than supervision: 'someone's there with me, either jazzing me up or I'm jazzing them up'. The rep agreed with the reframe rather than defending the mechanism.

anchors.raw: And do tell me, is it like a, you know, two, three, $4,000 or is it 20 grand? Like there's a huge range here, you know what I mean? And I'm sorry, I'm just, I can't drop 20 grand for this.
anchors.note: The prospect set his own ceiling at $20,000 before hearing the number, which made $6,000 land as relief rather than resistance — the rep leaned on exactly that: 'No, you don't have to... is 6K. So not 20.' The immediate reply was '6K up front... Let's get started, or?' There was zero price objection on this call; the blocker was purely liquidity.

anchors.raw: I'm working on, you know, all this stuff, trading. And I've always, I've wanted to trade and make it a profession since I was really a teenager... I'm in a program and, you know, I like the guy's strategy.
anchors.note: He is already inside a paid coaching programme in another domain while broke, which establishes both a willingness to buy structured coaching and a precedent for prioritising it over cash comfort. The rep never used it.

anchors.raw: because through the week, I've had to engage a lawyer. If I want to try and get any time with my daughter, I've got to stump up a fiver. You're saying stump up six, I've got to stump up a fiver.
anchors.note: A $5,000 legal retainer to get access to his daughter is competing for the same commission cheque as the $6,000 fee, and the prospect said the two sums out loud in the same breath. This is the real anchor on the call and it is not a competitor — it is a claim on the money that no discount or plan can beat.

unmet_demand.want: Weekly 48-hour to 5-day water fasts kept in place alongside the training programme, with an electrolyte protocol
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep endorsed the practice socially rather than answering it — 'Trevor's going to love that... he loves fast' — and deferred the actual protocol question to the onboarding call. Whether multi-day fasting is compatible with a loaded kettlebell block was never established, and the prospect had already named the risk himself: 'sometimes you get lightheaded'.

unmet_demand.want: Accountability without a group — peer energy rather than being watched by a community
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The accountability pillar is presented as Trevor's app check-ins plus the Skool community and a weekly group workout. The programme almost certainly serves this through the 1-1 relationship with Trevor, but nobody said so; the rep agreed with the prospect's objection instead of separating the two mechanisms.

unmet_demand.want: A way to start now on the money he could actually access — $500 within a week or $1,000 within two, with the balance at commission
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep declined to structure it and pushed the start to 21 August. Payment plans and $100-$500 deposits demonstrably exist at this company — the 07/03 team meeting has the manager coaching both — so this is a want the offer already serves that the rep did not use.
